issue.description:
Plan sections: "State & reliability" and "Testing & validation" (AS-3/AS-4) in docs/plan/plan.md.

hasTranscriptAdvanced() in daemon/reconcile.ts assumes transcript entries carry a numeric epoch-ms timestamp and types like user_message or a top-level role field. Real Claude Code transcript JSONL entries carry ISO-8601 string timestamps (e.g. 2026-06-20T12:52:29.993Z), top-level type of user/assistant with role nested under message.role, plus non-message lines (file-history-snapshot, mode, progress).

Consequence: the guard (entryTime <= lastStuckAt) compares an ISO string to a number, which is NaN-false, so the time filter never skips pre-stuck entries; the assistant entry that just produced the Stop matches (entry.type === "assistant") and the function returns true. Every real stuck session is therefore dequeued on the next reconcile tick (5s). The synthetic fixtures in test-walking-skeleton.sh use numeric timestamps, which is why AS-3/AS-4 pass while real usage is broken.

Fix:
- Parse timestamps robustly: Date.parse for ISO strings, pass through numbers.
- Only treat entries strictly newer than last_stuck_at as progress.
- Recognize the real entry shape (type user/assistant, message.role) and ignore snapshot/mode/progress lines.
- Update fixtures to the real transcript format (preferred) while keeping tests deterministic.
- Cleanup: daemon/reconcile.ts imports TranscriptEntry from daemon/types.ts (not exported there) and re-declares a local interface of the same name; remove the bogus import and keep one definition.

Acceptance criteria:
- New fixture test using real-format JSONL (ISO timestamps, nested message) shows: (a) a session stays queued while the transcript tail is only its pre-stuck assistant message; (b) appending a real-format user entry timestamped after the stuck time dequeues it within one sweep.
- test-walking-skeleton.sh AS-1..AS-7 still pass.
issue.title: Reconcile loop misparses real Claude Code transcripts - stuck sessions falsely dequeued within one 5s sweep

issue.description:
bin/trailboss-bootstrap injects a synthetic Stop event for every tmux pane whose
pane_current_command == "claude" that isn't already in the daemon's queue — with no
check for whether that pane is actually idle/waiting vs. actively mid-turn. It runs
automatically on every bin/trailboss-start.

daemon/tmux-detector.ts already implements the right check elsewhere in this same
repo: a quiet-threshold (TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS, default 30s) plus
capture-pane output-hash comparison to decide a pane is actually stuck, not just
running claude. trailboss-bootstrap should reuse that same
quiescence/output-hash logic (or shell out to the detector's single-pane check)
before injecting a synthetic Stop, instead of treating "command == claude" as
sufficient.

Concrete failure scenario: operator has N active Claude Code sessions genuinely
mid-turn (e.g. the 13 NATO-named tmux sessions alpha..mike observed live on
2026-07-20) and runs trailboss-start (e.g. after the systemd migration in ADR-1,
or just a fresh dashboard attach) — bootstrap would queue all N as "stuck", none of
which the operator actually needs to act on, defeating the FIFO signal-to-noise the
whole tool exists to provide.

Files: bin/trailboss-bootstrap, daemon/tmux-detector.ts (reference implementation
of the quiet-threshold check to reuse)
issue.title: trailboss-bootstrap flags any running claude pane as stuck, not just idle ones

## Alternative for: Starvation alert: beads invisible in 
Original bead: trailbos-9b927194

In /home/coding/trail-boss (bead-rs backend per .needle.yaml — use `bead`, never `br`), close the detector blind spot recorded in the trailbos-0c664d83 verification notes. Root cause: `bead list --ready` (bead-rs frontier) does not apply pluck's `exclude_labels` (deferred/human/blocked, per ~/.needle/config.yaml), so `detectBeadStarvation()` in daemon/reconcile.ts:565 computes `excludedBeads` from an open-vs-ready ID diff that reads excluded=0 in exactly the cycles pluck holds open beads out by label, then returns null at the `excludedCount === 0` early return. A workspace can therefore be silently unclaimable indefinitely — including holds whose rationale has expired (a `quarantine-until:<ts>` label in the past, or the blocker the deferral waited on now closed) — with no alert ever firing, which is the recurrence this false-positive alert family (trailbos-317b7ae2, trailbos-9b927194 and duplicates) was about. A live deliberate hold classifies deliberate=true and is auto-closed by the existing benign branch in `decideStarvationAlertAction` (daemon/reconcile.ts:963), so no new alert noise; an expired hold (quarantine timestamp past, or referenced blocker closed) classifies deliberate=false so the alert fires naming the stale hold as evidence. Constraints: do NOT remove, add, or mutate any operator-applied label in this task — reversing the deliberate `deferred` hold from commit 290e138 remains an operator decision; this changes only what the detector can see. Acceptance: extend test-starvation-detection.sh with (a) a fixture where all open beads carry `deferred` with a future quarantine-until → detector reports excluded>0, lifecycle action is close/benign, no alert bead created; (b) same fixture with quarantine-until in the past → validateStarvationAlert actionable and the alert evidence names the expired hold; (c) the existing test-7 zero-field suppression regression still passes. issue.description:
## Alternative for: Starvation alert: beads invisible in 
Original bead: trailbos-8cae488d

The detector already decides mechanically whether starvation exists (detectBeadStarvation() in daemon/reconcile.ts), whether a diagnostic is actionable (validateStarvationAlert()), and how to remediate it (checkpoint flush, dead-worker assignee clearing). What it never does is manage the alert beads themselves: createStarvationAlertBead() files a fresh bead on every failed recovery with no dedup (a persistent starvation would file one per 60s cycle), and nothing closes an alert when the condition resolves — every false positive to date (trailbos-8cae488d, trailbos-17befd15, trailbos-972e9ae8, tb-bctb, tb-67rg, tb-29cx, tb-5oiy, tb-11yy) required a hand-run investigation and a hand close.

Implement alert-lifecycle reconciliation in daemon/reconcile.ts and wire it into the existing 60s startStarvationDetection loop:

1. Before filing a new alert, list open beads carrying the starvation-alert label (`bead list --status open --json`, filter on labels).
2. Run one fresh detectBeadStarvation() for the workspace root.
3. Decision rule per existing open alert bead:
   - CLOSE as false positive when any of: the live diagnostic is recovered; validateStarvationAlert() rejects it (covers the blank-workspace/0-open/0-excluded shape of trailbos-8cae488d); or the ready frontier is non-empty with every excluded bead classifying to a known expected cause via classifyExcludedBead() (deferred/umbrella/split-child/manual-blocked — the tb-bctb 'all beads label-filtered' shape). Close with `bead close <id> --reason` quoting the evidence: live counts, ready-frontier result, and the classification causes.
   - REFRESH when starvation genuinely persists: do not file a duplicate — update the existing bead in place with fresh counts, timestamp, recovery attempts, and exclusion reasons. Use read-modify-write (`bead update --notes` REPLACES notes, never appends) and `--if-revision` for optimistic concurrency.
4. Invariant: at most one open starvation-alert bead per workspace at any time.
5. Extend test-starvation-detection.sh with three cases: (a) a resolved diagnostic closes an open alert with evidence in the close reason; (b) a persistent starvation refreshes the existing bead instead of creating a second one; (c) the exact trailbos-8cae488d zero-field diagnostic both fails validateStarvationAlert() at emission and, if one is already open, gets auto-closed as a false positive.

Notes for the executor: restart the systemd `trailboss-daemon` user service after editing reconcile.ts so the loop picks up the change; commit directly to main with explicit paths; close the implementing bead via `bead batch --json '[{"op":"close","id":"<id>","reason":"..."}]'` (br close is unreliable). Acceptance: after this lands, no starvation alert bead ever needs a hand-run triage — the loop that detects starvation also resolves its own alerts, which is exactly the work the operator was doing by hand.

---

Implemented mechanical exclusion-cause classification in detectBeadStarvation() (commit b4819b3, pushed to origin).

What changed in daemon/reconcile.ts:
- Open vs ready are diffed by ID set, not count subtraction; ready_beads is |open and ready| so the counts always satisfy validateStarvationAlert even when a bead is claimed between the two CLI snapshots.
- classifyExcludedBead() derives each excluded bead's cause from bead data alone, per the spec: (a) in_progress -> the assignee's most recent heartbeat state+age, falling back to the claiming worker found in .beads/events.jsonl; (b) open+assignee -> dead-assignee candidate; (c) unclosed blockers listed with each blocker's status, read from the dependencies field of the full bead list (the `bead dep` subcommand only add/removes edges and cannot list, so the JSON field is the mechanical source); (d) manual_blocked -> recorded as deliberate, no further digging. - Classification is appended to each bead's notes via `bead update --notes`, once per distinct cause-set per daemon process.

1. `bead update --notes` REPLACES the notes field rather than appending (probed in a throwaway bead workspace). issue.description:
bin/trailboss-status fetches /status with --max-time 0.1; on curl failure it falls
back to {"stuckCount":-1}, but the python parser only prints when count > 0, so
count=-1 (daemon down) and count=0 (queue empty) both render as a blank status
segment. The operator (and the TUI's own header/status bar, which polls the same
endpoint) cannot tell "all caught up" from "the whole tool is dead" by looking at
the ambient indicator — which is exactly the failure mode observed live during the
2026-07-20 artifact-improvement audit (daemon down, 13 active tmux sessions, no
visible signal).

Fix: bin/trailboss-status should render a distinct glyph/color for daemon-unreachable
(e.g. "✗ down") vs stuck-count (e.g. "⚠ 3") vs healthy-empty (blank or "✓"). Same
distinction should exist in tui/model.go's status bar (already has a "daemon:
unreachable ✗" state per docs/plan/plan.md Phase 8 — verify it renders correctly and
apply the equivalent fix to the bash status-line segment which currently does not).

References: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (daemon persistence). This bead is
independent of ADR-1 and should ship regardless — a reliable dead-daemon indicator
is needed even after daemon persistence is hardened, for the restart window and for
any other outage cause.

Files: bin/trailboss-status, tui/model.go

issue.description:
Trail Boss is entirely pull-based today: the status-line segment and TUI both
require the operator to be attached to a tmux client to see anything. If the
operator is away from the terminal entirely (not attached to any tmux client —
e.g. commuting, sleeping), stuck sessions pile up silently with zero notification
until they next attach. This is the same "human on the loop, not in it" gap the
tool otherwise solves for in-session switching, just not solved yet for the
case of "not in any session."

telegram-claude-bridge.service already runs on this host as a systemd --user
service with a working outbound notification channel — reuse that integration
(or a similar one) to fire a message when the queue's stuck count crosses a
configurable threshold (e.g. >=1, or after N minutes at the head unresolved) and
has not already sent one for the current head item, so it doesn't spam per-event.
Rate-limit / dedupe so a burst of Stop events doesn't produce a burst of messages.

Files: daemon/index.ts or a new daemon/notify.ts, integration point with
telegram-claude-bridge (check ~/telegram-claude-bridge for its send-message
interface/API)

issue.close_reason: Already implemented in commit e399956 on 2026-08-27. Client-side retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts) and bounded spool (100 lines max) with daemon-side replay on startup fully addresses the daemon restart window gap.
issue.description:
.claude/trailboss-emit.sh POSTs each hook payload once and always exits 0 (hooks
must not block/fail the CLI), so any POST that lands while the daemon is
restarting (e.g. during the systemd auto-restart window from ADR-1, RestartSec
plus daemon boot time) is silently and permanently dropped for that event. The
reconcile loop backstops *stuck* detection on restart by re-scanning transcripts,
but a dropped UserPromptSubmit (dequeue signal) has no equivalent backstop within
the same restart window — worst case a resolved session stays queued until the
next reconcile sweep notices the transcript advanced.

Add a small bounded local retry/spool in trailboss-emit.sh: on POST failure, retry
once or twice with a short backoff (still must stay fast enough not to block the
hook noticeably), or append the failed payload to a small local queue file that a
daemon-side "replay on startup" step consumes. Keep it bounded (e.g. last N
failed events, drop oldest) so a long outage doesn't grow it unbounded — the
reconcile loop is still the authoritative backstop for the stuck-detection side
per docs/plan/plan.md's "State & reliability" section.

References: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (this bead is the client-side hardening
follow-on named in that ADR's Consequences section).

Files: .claude/trailboss-emit.sh, daemon/index.ts, daemon/reconcile.ts
issue.notes:
Task already completed in commit e399956 (2026-08-27). Implementation includes:
- Client-side exponential backoff retry (3 attempts: 0ms, 100ms, 300ms)
- Spool to ~/.trailboss-spool.jsonl after retries exhausted
- Bounded spool: max 100 lines, drops oldest if exceeded
- Daemon-side replaySpool() processes spooled events on startup
- Integrated into startup sequence after stuck-direction reconcile
- All requirements from bead description satisfied
issue.title: Bound client-side retry for dropped hook POSTs during daemon restart window

detail.reason: Completed bounded client-side retry for dropped hook POSTs during daemon restart window. Added persistent failure logging to ~/.local/share/trailboss/failed-events.jsonl for events that fail to replay from spool. Full reliability chain now in place: (1) exponential backoff retry on POST failure (3 attempts: 0ms, 100ms, 300ms), (2) spool to local file if all retries fail, (3) daemon replays spooled events on startup, (4) failed replays logged persistently for forensics, (5) max queue size bounds prevent unbounded growth. All other components already implemented via prior work (trailboss-emit.sh retry + spool, daemon replaySpool function).

Task completed successfully. Audit confirmed: (1) NO CORS headers exist in daemon/index.ts - none to remove. (2) Server correctly binds to loopback only (127.0.0.1:4000). (3) Plan-specified invariant tests already existed in test-invariants.sh and comprehensively cover all three invariants: loopback-only binding, no send-keys synthesization, and CORS rejection. Integrated invariant tests into the acceptance test suite by adding invocation to test-walking-skeleton.sh. All trust boundary and input guarantee invariants now tested as part of Phase 6 acceptance criteria. Changes committed and pushed.

Auto-jump on resolve implementation already existed in daemon/index.ts (lines 16, 405-443). Added missing AS-9 acceptance test and documentation for TRAILBOSS_AUTO_JUMP environment variable. The feature is now complete with test coverage and user-facing docs in README.md and CLAUDE.md.

Implemented trailboss-doctor healthcheck command. The bin/trailboss-doctor script diagnoses common Trail Boss issues: daemon status (systemd unit active/reachable), tmux integration (TMUX env var, pane tracking), hook configuration (Stop/PermissionRequest/SessionStart/SessionEnd), database state (existence, stats, orphaned entries, spool), and systemd unit (file exists, enabled for auto-start). Provides color-coded output with actionable error messages for each check.

Notification system fully implemented and tested. Created daemon/notify.ts with background checker, rate limiting (1hr cooldown), deduplication, and graceful degradation. Fixed getHead() to include reason field. Added TRAILBOSS_PORT env var support. Created test-notification.sh acceptance test that validates notification delivery, cooldown behavior, and message format. Daemon restarted and successfully picking up environment variables (TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, TELEGRAM_PROXY_URL, etc.). All tests passing.

Implemented --verbose flag for 'bead list' that provides detailed diagnostics
about why beads may be excluded from the ready frontier. The logging includes:

1. Total open beads statistics (count and breakdown by state)
2. Filter criteria applied (status, assignee, ready/blocked flags, limit)  
3. Complete SQL query executed with parameters shown
4. Result set size with starvation warning when empty
5. Per-bead exclusion analysis showing exactly why each open bead is excluded
   (has assignee, manually blocked, blocked by dependencies, resource conflicts)
